answer: Nested agent lineage. Each new agent identity must present a parent-signed delegation chain rooted in one founding root; the registry assigns every root a distinct onyx slot that caps descendant count. Duplicate spawning splits this quota, so a Sybil cluster burns slots fast and stalls. Roots inherit a shared whisper channel only if their chains diverge within one island namespace, making copycat trees collide visibly. Cost: attacker must acquire fresh roots at market price, not clone cheap keys.
